2464.text: Director Riddlevox put me in charge of the Union's shredder development program. Few months on the job and I'm already in hot water! I could use your help, $n!

2527.text: Greetings.  I'm an undead mage trainer, and you're a mage.
2527.text1: Greetings.  I'm an undead mage trainer, and you're a mage.

2529.text: Greetings, $c.  Are you here to learn of the hidden arts?
2529.text1: Greetings, $c.  Are you here to learn of the hidden arts?

2545.text1: It is not yet your time. I shall aid your journey back to the realm of the living... for a price.

2660.text: Naralex sleeps again!$b$bLong ago, Naralex journeyed to this cavern with the honorable goal of entering the Emerald Dream and regrowing the Barrens into a lush forest. His focus waned and his thoughts became tainted by serpentine visions.$b$bNow, reptilian beasts seep from his dreams to the land. He must be awoken from the nightmare or he will be forever lost, and a great evil unleashed.$b$bOnly after his corrupted servants, the Fanglords, have been slain can I perform the awakening ritual.

2661.text: The Fanglords are dead! All hope is not lost!$b$bThe awakening ritual is quite complex, however. It cannot be done alone.$b$bI will handle all of the necessary preparations but I will need you to protect me. The nightmares summoned from Naralex's journey through the Emerald Dream prove to be quite formidable. Without your help, this mission is doomed.$b$bWhen you are ready to defend me, say the word, and I shall lead the way to Naralex's chamber.

2824.text: Rest your weary bones for a spell.
2824.text1: Rest your weary bones for a spell.

2825.text: As the wind on the plains, you are always welcome here.
2825.text1: As the wind on the plains, you are always welcome here.

3003.text: If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.
3003.text1: If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.

3344.text: I don't get too many Skinners in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.
3344.text1: I don't get too many Skinners in here looking for training, but I guess I could teach you something if you're ready.

3486.text:
Don't blame you for taking up fishing.  Mulgore has some the best fishing spots in Southern Kalimdor and Mountaintop Bait & Tackle on the high rise has all of the gear you'll need to take advantage of it.

3901.text: Hello, $n! If you don't see it in my shop, chances are good I can get it!

3961.text: Want to be a smith? Want to forge blades to gut your foe? Hammers to crush his skull? Aye I can help, and gladly too if there is blood to be shed from it.

4139.text: Welcome to Blue Moon Odds and Ends, $c.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

4350.text: Although we call this land the Barrens, to one who knows where to look this place teems with life.

4486.text: Interesting, interesting... I know of a druid that lives atop the hill above the Wailing Caverns, $n. She might be able to tell you more about this shard you have found.$B$BNow, I must get back to work!

4617.text: Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.
4617.text1: Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.

4619.text: I guarantee this bank's security with my own blood, is that good enough for you?
4619.text1: I guarantee this bank's security with my own blood, is that good enough for you?

4621.text: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?
4621.text1: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?

4635.text: The earth keeps many secrets, $c; it is our duty to ensure that those that must remain a secret for the good of all stays as such.
4635.text1: The earth keeps many secrets, $c; it is our duty to ensure that those that must remain a secret for the good of all stays as such.

4769.text: Godan's Runeworks is where you'll go.  Look for it on the west end of The Drag, right next to the Valley of Wisdom.
4769.text1: Godan's Runeworks is where you'll go.  Look for it on the west end of The Drag, right next to the Valley of Wisdom.

4792.text: We have our duties, $c.  Duties to the Horde.

4963.text: Of course there's no danger in everything catching flames and exploding like a huge helium bomb. This baby will get you to Undercity faster and safer than any boat, and the view is truly breathtaking. Speaking of breath, smoking is not allowed while on board the zeppelin, and fire spells are banned from being cast during the trip.

4965.text: My brother said we could make great money with this trade route, but he didn't tell me I would be the one living on this side. If you come back this way on the Zeppelin, could you bring me something to eat? They sell some of the finest meat in Orgrimmar, and I sure could use something that didn't die weeks before it stopped moving.

They sell some of the finest meat in Orgrimmar, and I sure could use something that didn't die weeks before it stopped moving.

5492.text: Every scrap used makes us less wasteful and brings us closer to the Earth Mother.  Mooranta can show you the way.  Seek her just outside the Thunder Bluff Armorers on the middle rise.
5492.text1: Every scrap used makes us less wasteful and brings us closer to the Earth Mother.  Mooranta can show you the way.  Seek her just outside the Thunder Bluff Armorers on the middle rise.

5536.text: The liquids and mixtures all bubble and spasm as you approach. Next to the equipment lies a large pair of tongs that look as though they would be adequate for dropping in samples of ooze.$B$BThere is safety gear present, but it appears to be dusty and well-ignored.$B$BYou don't think touching anything would be wise.

5739.text: I hear one comment about waterfowl, and you will be eating through a tube.

5752.text: I hope to one day forge weapons and armor from the bones of my enemies.

5753.text: You are not trying to kill the anvil with your hammer, you are trying to create a weapon to kill your foes with. Let me show you what you are doing wrong.

5877.text: You look for Martha Alliestar.  She on inner ring of The Apothecarium.

5942.text: I came to the Crossroads from the south seeking help, $c, but I find only cowards who turn their backs on me--even the mighty Thork insults me so. He is a good leader, but his dismissal of my plea causes me greater anger.$B$BHe claims my rage makes me hasty--that it clouds my judgement--but I will not rest until I have vengeance!

5943.text: I thank you, $n. Your dedication to my plea gives rest to my lost wife's spirit, and for that I could never repay you enough.$B$BI cannot say that my hatred will ever cease for the quilboar, but it is satiated for now.$B$BNow I must begin to rebuild my life.

5963.text1: The body is that of a female orc warrior.$B$BIt is clear that she died in battle, probably against the quilboar in the area.

5965.text1: You turn the body over and see the marks from blades and spells upon the deceased orc--her armor all but destroyed, her hair matted to her face.$B$BBased on Mankrik's description of her, there is no doubt in your mind that this was his wife.$B$BHe will be upset by the news, but you are sure he should know the truth.

5969.text: Welcome to the Crossroads, $c. My name is Thork--I lead the defenses here in the name of the Warchief.$B$BPlease, feel free to make yourself at home. As long as you mind your business, no one should have any problem with you taking up some space.$B$BThere are many threats to our safety here. If you've already become familiar with the lay of the land, speak to the others here--perhaps they have tasks for you to do.

6016.text: The Valley of Trials will temper even the weakest into a warrior worthy to join the Horde. Those who cannot rise to its tests will be left to bake in the scorching desert sun.

6075.text: You! $R! Come here. <snort>$B$BTime is short, and my end <snort> is near. Mangletooth shall win; you will see. <snort>$B$BMy capture can still aid <snort> my people. The Razormane tribe is more powerful than the Bristlebacks!$B$BThe Horde looks to find out who leads the raids on their people. You <snort> shall aid Mangletooth in return for the information only I know. Mangletooth can help you! <snort> But you must help Mangletooth.

6077.text: My hatred is strong <snort>, but the time is right to tell you a tale, $r.$B$BLong ago a battle took place between gods. Agamaggan, our great boar god, fell to the earth after being defeated in the War of the Ancients, his blood raining down and his bones torn asunder. <snort>$B$BGreat thorns reached up out of the earth where his blood touched the ground, and his skull adorns one of the caverns to the south.

6267.text: Heya mon.  Go talk to mah Master Gadrin right over there.  Take care of that Zalazane crazy for him and I fix ya right up!

6268.text: Ya mon, I be Gadrin's assistant.  Dis here volunteer work be my way of gettin through Witch Doctor School.  Since you help him, I help ya for free.  Whatcha need fixin?

6566.text: On the east side of Razor Hill, behind the barracks is where you will find Dhugru Gorelust.
6566.text1: On the east side of Razor Hill, behind the barracks is where you will find Dhugru Gorelust.

6591.text: There's a Skinning Trainer in Orgrimmar.  To get there head north up the road out of Razor Hill.  Ask an Orgrimmar Grunt for directions when you arrive.
6591.text1: There's a Skinning Trainer in Orgrimmar.  To get there head north up the road out of Razor Hill.  Ask an Orgrimmar Grunt for directions when you arrive.

7057.text: The skinners usually take all their hides into Ironforge to dry out.  Why don't you head there and see if you can find one to train ye?
7057.text1: The skinners usually take all their hides into Ironforge to dry out.  Why don't you head there and see if you can find one to train ye?

7214.text: Well met, $c. You may speak to me unless you have direct business with my mistress Magatha.$B$BI deal with most of her tasks for her so she can concentrate on more important matters. Perhaps there are some things we could discuss before you seek audience with her?

7216.text: Please, feel free to speak to me anytime, $n. You have served Magatha well. I am sure she will call upon you in the future.

7217.text: Do not presume to speak to me as though you are my equal, $c. Sylvanas is my queen, and I will do as she bids.$B$BIf you do not show the proper respect, I assure you, we can find a more than suitable place for you in the Nether.$B$BBut there is no reason we cannot have words if you wish to aid the Dark Lady...

7218.text: All members of the Horde are equal in my eyes, $n. We have all suffered many burdens, and if it were not for wisdom and honor, then we would be no better than the Scourge or my people while our blood was tainted by the demon Mannoroth.$B$BIt is your duty to aid the Horde and to defend our way of life. But it is also your duty to know when quarter and compassion should be given to friend and foe alike.$B$BUnderstand this well. This is the new Horde, not some demon-spawned army who lack freewill.

7228.text: Listen closely to what you are told and do not quickly trust, or distrust.  For even friends serve their own ends, $c.$B$BOur great Warchief knows this, and to prove that there are warlocks within the Horde who do not wish to destroy it from within or gain control over it, I have volunteered to aid our young leader in anyway I can.

7260.text: It would be wise to explain to you the depths at which our enemies will go to to hide themselves under our noses.$B$BKnow this first and foremost: our enemy is the Shadow Council. No matter what task I give you, or who I ask you to act against, know that one simple fact.$B$BMany cults exist within the Council, but only to hide its actions against the foolish.$B$BGroups like the Burning Blade, the Argus Wake, and the Searing Blade are all tools of the Council. Consider them one and the same.

7262.text: Ah, one of our own. It is good to see our numbers are growing so rapidly that I can no longer keep track of the faces of our members.$B$BThat fool Thrall thinks I am working hard to cleanse the image of warlocks and prove we are his servants. Idiot! The Burning Legion will make ash of this entire world after it drains it completely.

7263.text: Naive fool. The Burning Blade IS the Shadow Council! There are many cults and organizations under the Council's rule, but all of them are just extensions of their will. I may lead the Burning Blade, but I am still just as much a pawn to the Council as you are to me!$B$BLook at the Searing Blade--most of them think they are becoming the next rising group of powerful warlocks that they will replace the Shadow Council.

7264.text: Haha! Save for their leaders--the satyr, Bazzalan, and the warlock Jergosh--yes, all of them. That is why I constantly send Thrall's worshippers at them. It gives Thrall the impression that I am weeding out the evil in the bowels of his great city. The victory is in reality two-fold: kill Thrall's faithful and test the strength of those in the Searing Blade to see if they are truly worthy of joining me.

7265.text: I will make it known to you. You are obviously already proving yourself in our ranks to become a lieutenant so quickly. Perhaps you can return to me later and I will have tasks for you. The council adores those skilled in the arcane, but servants of all kinds are always welcome, no matter their profession.

7448.text: Greetings, $c.  You are welcome in Nighthaven, as well as all of Moonglade.  The Cenarion Circle welcomes all beings who respect the authority and command of nature.$B$BWhile you are here, please be sure to preserve the balance in all things.  Disturbances are not welcome here, and our wardens are trained to cease all hostilities without question.

7451.text: Welcome, my $g brother : sister;.  If you are here to train, then I would be delighted to teach you.$B$BIt never hurts to reaffirm one's place within what I like to call the Great Balance.  As preservers of this balance, we must strive to continually keep our minds clear and our hearts strong.  Training helps us in this regard.
7451.text1: Welcome, my $g brother : sister;.  If you are here to train, then I would be delighted to teach you.$B$BIt never hurts to reaffirm one's place within what I like to call the Great Balance.  As preservers of this balance, we must strive to continually keep our minds clear and our hearts strong.  Training helps us in this regard.

7529.text: I train and guide young hunters in the traditions passed down many generations.

7534.text: I can teach you the finer points of Raptor Riding, provided you have enough gold to cover the lesson!
7534.text1: I can teach you the finer points of Raptor Riding, provided you have enough gold to cover the lesson!

7584.text: The times we live in are as fickle as the shifting winds, $c.  It is important to remember what is true and lasting in this world, and to preserve that.  Everything else is a waste.

7586.text: No other race on Azeroth has suffered as much as our people, $c. To laugh in the face of death has become second nature for all of us.

7659.text: The spirits have guided you to me. How may I be of service?
7659.text1: The spirits have guided you to me. How may I be of service?

7663.text: Da spirits be strong wit you, mon. What kin dis troll do for ya?
7663.text1: Da spirits be strong wit you, mon. What kin dis troll do for ya?

7707.text1: Nice to see a friendly face. I don't get much chitchat from Apothecary Johaan unless he wants something. He's been out of the grave too long. Someday I'll be like that, I hear. Creepy. Maybe by then I won't care.

7710.text: Once, it is true, I was human. What might otherwise be a shortcoming works to our advantage, $n, for I know human weaknesses intimately.

7733.text: I'm busy, $n. Tell Whuut to handle whatever it is. That young pup has been stewing all day long. He spends much more time like that, and he's going to hurt something.

7754.text: With Algernon to keep me supplied, I can do all my work here without hunting for a single herb. If I never have to see the wonders of nature again, it won't be too soon.

7817.text: I like to build stuff. Of course, I like to blow stuff up even more!

7818.text: You know who can really show you some things? Nogg! You go find him in Orgrimmar.

7819.text: I know a few things. You want me to show you?

7829.text: Hmm... well, I can't help you quite yet! You have to learn the basics first. Why don't you go see Sprite Jumpsprocket in Stormwind!

7834.text: You can learn from me in time... but not yet! Why don't you start out by talking to Sprite Jumpsprocket to my right here. You can check in with me after you've gotten your feet wet!

7843.text: Every day is a test, and this day is no different. If you pass this test, I will share some of my knowledge...

7859.text: Nice try, but you'll need some more experience before training with me! Back to the trenches!

7880.text: I do not have time to waste, stranger. State your business or be off!

7886.text: Throm-ka! What you looking for, stranger?

7961.text1: You like the rug? I killed and skinned the beast myself. May all the centaur fall as easily.

7962.text1: I have nothing more to teach you. Talk to Karolek if you wish to further your leatherworking skills.

7963.text1: Too bad we can't skin the humans and their allies. All that skin is just going to waste. Still, who'd want to wear the flimsy leather you could make out of it?

7964.text1: Skin, glorious skin. It holds your insides... in. You might've noticed my skin's not doing so well. To think I used to worry about my pores. Hardly any skin left to worry about these days. In a way, it's very freeing.

7965.text1: You've got the hang of it. I can't teach you any more, but talk to Arthur Moore, a Forsaken who works in the Rogues' Quarter of the Undercity. Tell him I sent you.

7966.text1: Before the plague came, I knew nothing about leather. Now I know enough to teach others. Death's left me with a lot of time on my hands.

7972.text: Even here in the wilds, you seek out learning. Your drive for knowledge is an admirable trait.

7974.text: Your talent is beyond my own, friend. Speak with Tarn here; his knowledge of leather is much greater than mine. I'm sure he would welcome another student.

7976.text: When I clawed my way out of the grave, I thought my family would welcome me with open arms. Instead, they drove me from the village, screaming in a language I could no longer understand.

7978.text: Take every word I say and commit it to memory. Until our enemies have been eradicated, we must never shirk a chance to further our knowledge. Reinforce your armor, and never relax your guard.

8007.text: I do not offer apprentice training. Look for the tauren Waldor in the Wailing Caverns, here in the Barrens. He can assist you with whatever you need.

8013.text: I am pleased with your progress so far. Surely the Earth Mother has inspired your hands.

8018.text: We're pretty far from anything I'd call civilization here, at least until the Horde can send us more reinforcements. You must really like working with leather.

8023.text: The twists and turns of Orgrimmar are designed to thwart invaders. Can you imagine how quickly one of those puny gnomes would get lost in here? Ha! If it was lucky, I'd track it down and keep it as a pet.

8049.text1: It's been so long since I was a novice myself that I don't think I'd be the best teacher for you. Try talking to Tarn or Mak, right over there. One of them should be able to answer your questions.

8071.text: We use many animal pelts and skins in our creations.

8074.text: No part of the animals we hunt is wasted.

8094.text: Greetings.  Our bats are well trained and fed.  You'll not find faster.

8095.text: How may I be of service?

8096.text: Greetings, and welcome.  I am not very good at smiling, but trust me; I am happy to serve you.

8111.text: My wind riders are trained to fly quickly through the hot Barrens air.

8116.text: When mounted on the back of a wind rider, one sees that its reputation for strength and speed is well earned.

8120.text: Have a look at my meats, friend.  You won't want to go out into the Barrens without a good stock of provisions.

8122.text: You haven't lived until you've looked down on the world from the back of a wind rider.

8162.text1: Welcome to our tent. May I assist you?

8190.text: Cloth is okay. Personally I prefer to work with human skin.

8289.text: You know enough to be dangerous, but you still look like you need training to me $n.
8289.text1: You know enough to be dangerous, but you still look like you need training to me $n.

8293.text: $n, how may I further your training in the eyes of the Earth Mother?
8293.text1: $n, how may I further your training in the eyes of the Earth Mother?

8364.text: I am an orc of medicine, $r. If you have come here to learn, I shall do my best to teach.

8402.text: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.
8402.text1: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.

8453.text1: As a mage, you are one of a select group that can conjure a portal to transport you back to this very place.  I can teach you if you are ready.

8455.text: As a mage, you are one of a select group that can conjure a portal to transport you back to this very place.  I can teach you if you are ready.

8457.text: As a mage, you are one of a select group that can conjure a portal to transport you back to this very place.  I can teach you if you are ready.

8810.text: Here to learn how to wield a new weapon, or just to waste my time?

8862.text: Heya mon.  You come right place learn how ta wield a new weapon.

8864.text:
Ansekhwa, da tauren weapon master, is on da Thunder Bluff lower rise.  He teach one and two-handed maces, staves and guns.

Archibald, da undead weapon master in da War Quarter of da Undercity, train good with crossbows, daggers, one and two-handed swords and polearms.

Sayoc, da ugly orc right here, can teach da ways of bows, daggers, fist weapons, one and two-handed axes and thrown weapons mon.

8866.text: I would be honored to train you in the use of the weapons that I have mastered should you have the ability to learn within you.

8873.text: I suppose you are here to be trained in the use of a new weapon?  Make it fast, I'm very busy!

9551.text: Greetings and salutations, hero!  I have the latest news from both continents and points beyond for your consideration.
9551.text1: Greetings and salutations, hero!  I have the latest news from both continents and points beyond for your consideration.

9557.text: I can teach you fishing skills.
9557.text1: I can teach you fishing skills.

9667.text: Greetings young one, and welcome to Thunder Bluff.  You'll find safe refuge from the burdens of the world here.  All denizens of the Horde are welcome here.$B$BThe spirits of the present and past come alive here in this sacred place, my friend.  Honor them, and in doing so honor yourself.

9685.text: Cooking is a life long pursuit and I see we share the same passion!
9685.text1: Cooking is a life long pursuit and I see we share the same passion!

9688.text: I can teach you how to cook!
9688.text1: I can teach you how to cook!

9701.text: I can train you in First Aid techniques.
9701.text1: I can train you in First Aid techniques.

9877.text: Are you interested in exploring one of these dungeons?
9877.text1: Are you interested in exploring one of these dungeons?

9891.text: Hail $g brother : sister;... I'd like a moment of your time, if I may.$B$BWe tauren have endured much in our trials and tribulations in establishing our homeland.  We now find ourselves in a dire shortage of cloth.  If you have the materials to spare, I ask that you please donate them.  You certainly would earn the gratitude of tauren everywhere in helping us out!

10029.text: Where can I send you today $c?

10030.text: Though the Crossroads seems to be the center of activity in The Barrens, I prefer the quietude of Camp Taurajo.  Where shall I send you?

10031.text: Many are the paths of the Earth Mother.  Wherever you decide to travel, may she watch over you.

10753.text: Where would you like to fly to?
10753.text1: Where would you like to fly to?

10863.text: War is upon us, $n.  It's time for every member of the Horde to answer the call and join the fight against the cowardly Alliance.

11113.text: Your quest to learn Draconic is futile, mortal. And why would you ever want to learn to speak in the ancient tongue? Baffling really...

212752.text: Knowledge is both tool and weapon to those with the will to use it.
212752.text1: Knowledge is both tool and weapon to those with the will to use it.

290402.text: You may not be a paladin, but you may yet find solace in the light should you seek it.
290402.text1: You may not be a paladin, but you may yet find solace in the light should you seek it.

292463.text1:
Why do they call me "The Breaker"?

Trust me, you don't want to know.

292961.text:
Professions are divided between two main categories: primary and secondary.

You are limited to a maximum of two primary professions at a time. You can abandon your skill in a primary profession at any time; however, the wealth of knowledge you gathered for it will be lost. If you choose to return to your original profession, you will need to train from the basics and seek out recipes you previously acquired to refamiliarize yourself with them.

Secondary professions do not have such a limit. These skills tend to err towards self-sufficiency with your basic survival needs. You are free to train any or all of these, but may find fewer opportunities to turn a profit.

293818.text1: Care to learn how to gather leather from slain beasts? Or do you need some new tools?

296783.text: The Dark Lady has put the challenge forth. Now it is up to the Royal Apothecary Society to develop a new plague. We shall bring Arthas and his wretched army to their knees.

299234.text1: Praise to the Banshee Queen, it isn't often I have visitors out here.

299683.text: Hail and well met, traveler.$B$BI wish my arrival was met with good tidings but the realm of Dalaran is in need of aid from the kingdoms of the Alliance.

299703.text:
Unfortunately, the rumor of our plight is true. Disruptions to our leylines have unveiled a disturbance amongst the arcane forces of our city.

With Dalaran on the cusp of reopening its borders to our allies, we are in dire need of immediate solutions.

299774.text: <As you approach the enormous cyclone construct, you hear a faint buzzing emanating from beneath its massive armor plates. If you listen carefully, you think you might be able to hear a few words being formed but they are too distorted to make out.>
299774.text1: <As you approach the enormous cyclone construct, you hear a faint buzzing emanating from beneath its massive armor plates. If you listen carefully, you think you might be able to hear a few words being formed but they are too distorted to make out.>

300037.text: H-Hello. You'll have to excuse me, I'm used to your kind running from me.

300039.text:
That is... a very good question. I have a hard time remembering things, but I do remember something... "Engineer", perhaps? I think that's what, or who, I was.

Other than that, all I can seem to remember is soaring through the sky, then seeing a flash of lightning before things got very bumpy. Then... a crash.

It's been... a long time though. A very long time.

300042.text:
Oh, these things? I built them. My little friends helped me. I'm not very good at remembering things, but, um, I do know that at one point I used to build a lot of things. Big things! But then, like I said... I was here. The things I build aren't so big and impressive anymore. Still makes me h-happy, heh.

B-but... If you want, I can show you how to build things too!

300516.text1: Where to begin? Our home is failing. The wards have fallen and the three provinces have begun to drift apart. There was a time not long ago when the spires of Shen'dramar were visible from the western watchtower. No longer. The anchor pylons are weakening, and if the chains finally break...

300517.text1:
Why is this happening? Put simply, the spirits of the wind just... vanished. They were there one day, and they were gone the next. I can't quite describe the feeling that we windshapers felt when it happened. It was as if a great silence fell over all of us and then... a profound absence.

The petty wraiths you've likely encountered out there are just shades of the glory of the true spirits of wind. Non-sentient, aimless, and a far cry from the kindly spirits we lived in harmony alongside for thousands of years.

300518.text1:
Many disagree on this point. I believe that simple communication is the key. The songs of the wind rang so clearly to us when the spirits were still here. Since they left, it's grown quiet and our power as windshapers has weakened. 

However, there are those of us who can still hear something. A hushed tone. Fragments of a melody. Those that can still hear and see into the elemental planes must grow in strength. I believe that is the key to our salvation.

300519.text1:
The Cult? They are zealots and killers. They believe that we are being punished for some unspecific sin. The reality is that those that lead them are opportunists leftover from a dubious order of so-called "Priests" of Al'Akir, the Windlord. 

They now find themselves in a position to weaponize the fear of our people to consolidate their own power... and they have been quick to do so.

300520.text1:
In all of our years dealing with the wind spirits, at no point did they speak of the Windlord as a figure of reverence. They acknowledged the existence of a being named Al'Akir, but they avoided invoking his name, almost as if they feared him. 

Even if this Al'Akir is an all-powerful "Windlord" or ruler of the wind elementals, my centuries of communion with the spirits has convinced me that at the very least he is not universally loved amongst the denizens of Skywall. I fear that attempting to treat with Al'Akir could merely hasten our doom.

300521.text1:
You must remember that while this realm has been our home for millennia, we will always be somewhat alien to this place. We are not in the terrestrial world that birthed our people. We are in the realm of Skywall, a part of the elemental plane.

We arrived here as the guests of spirits with whom we found common cause in ages past. Now that we Shen'dorei find ourselves bereft of their presence--and potentially--their protection, there's no telling how the other denizens of this plane may perceive us.

300522.text1: Alas, I have prattled on long enough. Seek out my apprentice Ayessa Dawnsinger in the port of Valanaar if you find yourself out that way. She still hears the song--if only faintly. I am old and much of my power has left me. Ayessa represents the future of our people and the path we must now walk to survive. It's up to her and young skyborne such as yourself to carry the hopes for our people forward.

300626.text1: Greetings, $c. Do you come seeking the blessings of the Windlord?

300662.text: If you need training as a cook, I have a few tips and tricks I could pass on! Ho ho! Throw on an apron and let's get started!

300663.text1:
Greetings, child. I am Illaya Amberwind and I am the Elder Windshaper here on Zephras Isle. It's always nice to meet young new faces that make their way down from the grove.

Don't let this old shaman hold you up, no doubt you've got many adventures to see to. Do feel free to stop by later if you'd like.

300665.text1: I'm in charge of Shen'dar Village operations, and there's a lot of things to keep track of around here. Between bandits, cultists, and other random incidents that pop up, keeping this village afloat is a lot of work.

300678.text1: <Constable Aonda wears an intense look on her face, clearly deep in thought.>

300698.text: I can teach you to craft fine leather armor, if you have the aptitude.

300702.text1:
The clothcraft of the Shen'dorei is a harmonious imitation of the flowing, carefree currents of the winds. While the spirits have left us, and I know not when I may see them dance once more... I find great comfort in my art, if only as a distraction.

I can teach you to work the cloth as well, if you'd like to learn?

300714.text: <The corpse lying before you is covered in scorches and burn marks. He seems to be clutching something in his hand.>
300714.text1: <The corpse lying before you is covered in scorches and burn marks. He seems to be clutching something in his hand.>

300915.text:
Our kind are rare these days, but there are those who still dream in emerald amongst the shen'dorei.

Keep your eyes open in the forest. The right light can reveal that which is hidden, protected by the north wind.

301025.text1: As you likely know, the wind pylons gifted to us by the spirits serve as our anchor to the elemental plane of Skywall. They are failing, and our home is in danger.

301026.text1: When you find yourself in the port of Valanaar, seek out Ayessa Dawnsinger. She can tell you more.

301027.text1: The Al'Aketh cult continues to escalate their violence, and the High Order's magical meddling could hasten our doom if left unchecked.

301028.text1: The Windshapers possess the gift of skysight, and we are working tirelessly to find our lost elemental benefactors, so that they may guide us once again.

301029.text1: The shamanistic magic we know is greatly diminished since the spirits vanished, but we are resolute in our mission to bring them home once again.

301030.text1: We will not stop until we are able to discover what went wrong. We will find the strength we need to call the spirits back to us.

301031.text1: The future is uncertain for our people, but there is hope, and we have a plan...

301040.text1: If you are looking for more work, I'm sure there are some folks in town that are also looking for help with one task or another. Just ask around, you are bound to find something.

301355.text: My wife and I run the stormapple orchard in the lowlands, just to the west of Valanaar.

301356.text: Some years ago our farm was attacked by bandits. They took everything we had and left me bruised and bloody. The next season around the same time, they returned.

301357.text: They took most of our harvest again, but this time the bandit leader--Ferauu "the Bludgeon" as he's known--told us that every season they'd return and take twice as much as the previous year.

301358.text: We tried to petition the peacekeepers to come and help drive the bandits off, but they are stretched too thin just dealing with the cult and couldn't spare anyone.

301359.text: This year our yield is light and we can't hope to give them what they expect. The best case is that they simply kill us quickly. It's more likely they take everything we have and leave us to starve.

301362.text: I came to town to hire fighters to drive them off. I found one warrior who agreed to help, but he robbed me as soon as we were out of town and nearly beat me to death.

301364.text: At this point I'm too injured to leave this bed. I'm begging you, stranger. Travel to my orchard. Tell Aamelia what happened and help her survive this somehow. Please, stranger... help us.

301399.text1: The Windfield Orchard has seen better days...

301445.text: Aamelia, my dear. Where's Alvarion? Too afraid to come and face Ferauu, so he sent you?

301446.text1: Alvarion? Oh he's still in the hills with the peacekeepers, clearing out the rest of your lackeys. I'm sure they'll be along any minute and would love to see you.

301447.text: HA! A poor bluff! Ferauu has eyes and ears everywhere. I know that it's just you and this scrawny stranger here. You've had your fun putting down a few of my weaker recruits, but The Bludgeon is here now and the party is over. Time to pay up, with interest.

301448.text1: I'm done talking. Stranger, thanks for everything...

301449.text1: Aamelia raises her pitchfork, ready to fight.

301450.text1: Huh. Well that was... unexpected. I guess we know what that big lug's purpose is now. Let's head back to the house, stranger.

301455.text: <The man lying before you shifts uncomfortably. He's recovering from some very nasty wounds.>

301456.text: It's always great to see you, $n.

301460.text1: As you know, our way of life is in grave danger. Since the elementals vanished, our people have been in a state of steady decline.

301461.text1: The Al'Aketh are a symptom of this. In many ways they are a dark mirror into the hearts of the Windshapers. Many of us believe that we are to blame for the spirits leaving us.

301462.text1: Whatever the cause, we need to find a solution quickly before we tear ourselves apart. Tell me, what do you know of Kalimdor?

301463.text1: The cradle of our people is now part of an even larger world known as "Azeroth". There are those on Azeroth possessing a skysight so strong that they can pierce the heavens themselves to see beyond.

301464.text1: Shamans, much like myself, but orders of magnitude more powerful. This power and their knowledge of the elemental planes is the key to our survival.

301465.text1: In my own clumsy searching throughout the planes for signs of our elemental benefactors, I stumbled upon them...

301467.text1: An entire order of visionaries just like the Windshapers called The Earthen Ring. One of their leaders, a shaman named Muln Earthfury, has shown me much.

301468.text1: I have seen the way. We must return to Kalimdor, confer with this Earthen Ring. They will help us master the skysight so that we may call our elemental patrons back home.

301469.text1: However, this journey will be dangerous. We need strong, able-bodied young shen'dorei to join us as we explore this massive new world. Those just like you, in fact.

301470.text1: You do not need to agree to this now. When the time comes, however, please consider joining us in our expedition. Until we speak again... may the winds guide your path.

301916.text: <This cultist is dead. Upon close inspection, you notice that he seems to be clutching something to his chest, almost as if he was protecting it.>
301916.text1: <This cultist is dead. Upon close inspection, you notice that he seems to be clutching something to his chest, almost as if he was protecting it.>

302063.text1: With the cult running roughshod over most of the island with impunity, Lorthuna undoubtedly thinks we are on the back foot. We can use that overconfidence against her.

302064.text1: I believe that with a proper distraction at the shrine, a small force of Peacekeepers, Windshapers, and High Order should be able to push up a flank and break into the inner sanctum. From there, we take out the High Priestess herself and cut the head off the snake.

302065.text1: Go and speak with the leaders of the Windshapers and the High Order, respectively. They don't get along, but I think they can recognize that the bigger threat is the Al'Aketh. Get them to agree to the plan and then return here.

302067.text1: Greetings, I am Ayessa Dawnsinger, the current Grand Skyseer of the Windshapers. What may I do for you?

302089.text:
<Elaadrin eyes you with barely-contained hatred.> 

You would dare step foot into our sanctum after spilling High Order blood? You are very brave, or very stupid. The High Order does not forgive, nor do we forget.

Someday, you will pay for your crimes in blood.

302090.text:
Hmm, I see. Very well then, $c. The High Order will assist the Peacekeepers. Please inform Valennia that she can count on us for this fight.

<Elaadrin lowers his voice dangerously.>

Do not mistake our willing cooperation for any sort of clemency. You owe the High Order blood, and we always collect on our debts.

302093.text:
The Peacekeepers can't hope to muster the numbers needed for an outright assault on the shrine. Without the Windshapers and the High Order bolstering our numbers, we stand no chance. They both pledged their aid when we need it. Now is the time.

Unfortunately, some recent events have led to outright bloodshed between the two factions, and tensions are high.

How do you feel about a bit of diplomacy?
302093.text1:
The Peacekeepers can't hope to muster the numbers needed for an outright assault on the shrine. Without the Windshapers and the High Order bolstering our numbers, we stand no chance. They both pledged their aid when we need it. Now is the time.

Unfortunately, some recent events have led to outright bloodshed between the two factions, and tensions are high.

How do you feel about a bit of diplomacy?

302159.text1: <Valennia is severely wounded and is barely holding on to consciousness.>

302160.text1:
Most of the cultists at the Sanctum of Storms seem to have come out to respond to our attack. I never would have expected this to go so well. This was almost too easy...

I think that the Windshapers and High Order have made their push. Valennia should be with them. You should head inside and find her. We'll stay here and keep watch while Valennia and the others finish what they came here to do.

302443.text: We came as soon as we were told what was happening. The High Order is here to serve Zephras.

302444.text1: ...and the Windshapers. We are ready to support an assault on the Shrine, Valennia.

302445.text1: You have my thanks. Being truthful, however, this is going to be a dangerous gambit and we may not succeed. It's important you understand that this might be a one-way ride.

302446.text1: We understand. As it happens Elaadrin and I spoke. We made arrangements to send for... outside aid. It's unclear if they will be able to arrive in time to help, or if they will even arrive at all...

302447.text1: Outside... of Zephras? From the other provinces? We haven't had contact with the other islands for years...?

302448.text: It's... coming from a little further away than that. We'll explain on the way.

302449.text1: Very well then. Time is not with us so we should make ourselves ready. Thank you all for your aid. Zephras is in your debt.

302631.text1: Aonda is a good woman, and a true servant of Zephras Isle. It is my hope that you can quickly earn her trust and help her to keep Shen'dar Village safe. May the winds guide you, $n.

302649.text1: Go with the blessings of Al'Akir. But be warned; those that approach the Windlord's faithful under false pretense will quickly face His wrath.

302650.text: <The two cultists nearby are talking. You might be able to learn something if you hide behind this wardrobe and eavesdrop.>
302650.text1: <The two cultists nearby are talking. You might be able to learn something if you hide behind this wardrobe and eavesdrop.>

302705.text: I tell you lot, that forest is haunted! I SAW *hic* WHAT I SAW!

302706.text: If you don't believe me, go and see for yourself! Terrible windblown wraiths *hic*... forest spirits that will gnaw your ankles!

302707.text: There's even a terrible forest wraith! Dressed all in black and... evil looking! I tell you, it's a cursed place! *hic*

302807.text: If you have the aptitude for the druidic arts, I can train you.
302807.text1: If you have the aptitude for the druidic arts, I can train you.

302811.text:
The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.
302811.text1:
The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

If you have the proper aptitude as a hunter, I can give you the tools to survive the wilds.

303598.text1: Oh, and a word of warning before you head up to Shadowgale Forest. It's incredibly dangerous up there. Some even say it's haunted. Make sure you are prepared and well-equipped if you plan to make the trek.

303612.text: Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?
303612.text1: Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?

304010.text: What do you need of me, child of Zephras?

304012.text1: What may I do for you, fellow windshaper?

304299.text1: Lorthuna! Stop this madness. You don't know what bringing down the wards protecting Zephras will do. You could doom us all!

304303.text1: Ayessa... my former sister. How far you've fallen, keeping company with this High Order filth.

304304.text: I'll make this easy for you, witch. Stop what you are doing now and I will make your death swift. This is the last and best offer you will get from the High Order.

304307.text1: Bring the wards down? The wards have been down for days, fools. No, I am merely lighting a beacon... for the true servants of Al'Akir to follow.

304433.text1: Ahh... yes! The call has been answered. Meet your end with joy!

304441.text: Who dares call the Lord of the East Wind?

304443.text: So the rumors were true. My wayward brothers did well to conceal this place from the gaze of Al'Akir.

304445.text1: Yes! Yes! It is by my will that the way to Zephras is open to you! Bring me before your Windlord so that he may know who was the herald of his glory!

304447.text: You dare to command me, mortal? No, I think not. Begone, insignificant elf!

304448.text1: No! Never, I would never dare!

304449.text: Well, you certainly never will again, insect. Hah!

304452.text: Enjoy your remaining time as "guests" in my lord's realm until his judgement inevitably arrives. You'll know not when, but it is coming.

304454.text: Now that this wondrous realm is no longer hidden from us, you are going to enjoy getting to know the TRUE children of Skywall...

304558.text: Oh, enough of that crazy talk, swimmers. You are going to scare off the few customers we have with your drunken ghost stories!
304558.text1: Oh, enough of that crazy talk, swimmers. You are going to scare off the few customers we have with your drunken ghost stories!

304612.text: Welcome to Shen'dar Village, some of the best fishing this side of the mountain range. If you are looking to catch fish, I can teach you, for a price.

304707.text: This construct might as well be a paperweight. Someone stole some of its most important components.

304709.text: Replacement parts are hard to come by these days, with how few intact constructs we have left on the island.

304710.text: If you want to try and find the components we need, I won't stop you, but it might require more than a little bit of scavenging.

304712.text: Shrieklings tend to hoard shiny things in their lairs, so it's possible some construct parts may have ended up in the shriekling cave just west of Valanaar.

304713.text: Constructs used to help us trawl Windsong Lake and when the pylons started to fail, many fell into the depths. There may be usable parts on the lakebed if you are up for a swim.

304716.text: Lastly, the bandit highwaymen common in the Gustberry Lowlands are known to hoard a variety of junk at their camps. Construct parts are likely to be found among such loot.

304785.text: POWER RESTORED. READY TO RESUME FUNCTION.

304786.text: ONE MOMENT PLEASE. RECOGNITION. SHEN'DOREI. HIGH ORDER MAGISTER.

304788.text: Now we're getting somewhere. Construct, can you tell me who removed your components?

304792.text: Construct Parts?! Are you serious? Do you know what the Al'Aketh will do if they find us both here together? Begone with you, now. I will submit myself to your judgement later. It is not safe...

304793.text1: Belathaan... I thought we agreed to meet alone? I'd hate to think you intended to ambush me here, in the shadow of my shrine.

304794.text: No, no! Lorthuna, you do not understand. This windshaper is merely passing by. They did not come here with me!

304795.text1: It matters not. I think that I'll just have my pets kill the both of you and send your tongue back to Elaadrin as a warning to keep his little mages in Valanaar, where they belong.

304796.text: Lorthuna, be reasonable. Elaadrin sent me to discuss a path to peace and...

304797.text1: Enough. Goodbye, Belathaan and... whomever you are.

304798.text: I appreciate you bringing me Ayessa's assurances. With both the High Order and the Windshapers working with us against the greater threat, we stand a much better chance to thwart the Al'Aketh and whatever they have planned for Zephras.

304802.text: Oh, and for you in particular, $c. Our scouts learned of your involvement with what happened to the magister, Belathaan Brightwish. If we know, the High Order surely knows as well.

304803.text: The High Order are not likely to be understanding, accidental or not. There will be a reckoning. I can only hope that cool heads prevail between your faction and the High Order... at least until the crisis with the Al'Aketh is resolved.

305021.text: You don't look like much, but something tells me you are right. I think I'll just sit here a bit longer. Thanks for the chat, stranger.
305021.text1: You don't look like much, but something tells me you are right. I think I'll just sit here a bit longer. Thanks for the chat, stranger.

305106.text: Sorry that we are late, Ayessa.

305107.text: It took a bit of work to convince Archmage Rhonin to help me open that transplanar portal...

305108.text: Ansirem! This isn't how I expected our first meeting to go, but I'm glad you made it!

305109.text1: Nor is this how I envisioned our first meeting, Muln.

305110.text: Well if this isn't an inspirational sight. The little elves seem to have friends in... low places.

305111.text: We have no quarrel with you, Lord of the East Wind. Leave us in peace.

305112.text: Very well, mortals. For now enjoy your respite. I simply cannot wait to tell the Windlord about all that has transpired here. You will be seeing me again... very soon.

305131.text1: Empty threats, Elaadrin. Regardless of what happens to me now, my great work is done. Consider yourself lucky to be here at the eye of the storm, to witness the fruits of our labor.

305132.text: Wait... what is this place? How could such a place exist in the Windlord's realm?

305133.text: I think it's time for us to be leaving this place. I will open a portal to Valanaar.

305134.text1: Muln Earthfury of the Earthen Ring--the Windshapers would be happy to accept you as our guest.

305135.text: Yes, and you, Archmage Runeweaver. The High Order is eager to learn more of the Kirin Tor.

305158.text: Adventurer! High Order and Windshapers fighters just took the wind bridge to the other side!
305158.text1: Adventurer! High Order and Windshapers fighters just took the wind bridge to the other side!

305159.text: The bridge is unstable and keeps sputtering out. Wait here with me until it returns.
305159.text1: The bridge is unstable and keeps sputtering out. Wait here with me until it returns.

305160.text: Adventurer! The wind bridge leading to the other spire is unstable. You may need to wait here with me until it returns.
305160.text1: Adventurer! The wind bridge leading to the other spire is unstable. You may need to wait here with me until it returns.

305849.text: High Priestess, we are ready to carry out your will. I will move on the western watchtower, and Commander Cyclas will lead the attack on Shen'dar Village. Both will be ours by tomorrow.
305849.text1: High Priestess, we are ready to carry out your will. I will move on the western watchtower, and Commander Cyclas will lead the attack on Shen'dar Village. Both will be ours by tomorrow.

305850.text1: The great work is nearly complete, Skypriest Aanders. Your success here is vital.

305851.text: Of course, High Priestess. We are the instruments of your will. I only wish you could be here to witness our triumph firsthand.
305851.text1: Of course, High Priestess. We are the instruments of your will. I only wish you could be here to witness our triumph firsthand.

305852.text1: I am needed elsewhere for now and this represents but one piece on the gameboard. Do not fail me, Aanders.

305854.text: Do you seek the blessings of the Windlord?
305854.text1: Do you seek the blessings of the Windlord?

306261.text1: It appears the winds have brought you my way! I am happy to train you in the ways of cooking if you have the inclination to learn.

306274.text: Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?
306274.text1: Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?

306276.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.
306276.text1: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.

306575.text1: $n, ensure any allies with you are prepared to fight, and speak with me when you are ready to confront Lorthuna.

306593.text: <The gaze of the ranger standing before you is fixed on the enormous anchor pylon in the distance.>
306593.text1: <The gaze of the ranger standing before you is fixed on the enormous anchor pylon in the distance.>

307118.text:
<Before you lies the corpse of Jorel Windsinger.

Deep lacerations are cut into his legs, and lightning burns scorch his fur.

It is clear he put up a fight before succumbing to his wounds.>
307118.text1:
<Before you lies the corpse of Jorel Windsinger.

Deep lacerations are cut into his legs, and lightning burns scorch his fur.

It is clear he put up a fight before succumbing to his wounds.>

307316.text: The spirit of strength does not always refer to physical strength. To face adversity both from within and without is what it means to take my shape.

307915.text: Watch yourself. The High Order will not tolerate hostility in our lodge.
307915.text1: Watch yourself. The High Order will not tolerate hostility in our lodge.

309474.text:
<Before you lies a skyborne; his body is mangled and bruised but still recognizable. It is clear he met a gruesome end while attempting to flee.

It appears that all of his belongings are still on his body, and a half-filled crate nearby lies spilled on the ground.>

309779.text:
No fights goin' on today, pal. The Horde and the Alliance are too busy killin' each other out in the fields when there's perfectly good coin to be made doin' that in my arena! Go figure.

Come back when I get this place up and runnin'.

310718.text: Are you in need of a weapon, traveler? You'll not find a finer blade anywhere, I assure you.
310718.text1: Are you in need of a weapon, traveler? You'll not find a finer blade anywhere, I assure you.

310819.text: Even in death... I will persist.

312221.text: <Riaani seems to be intently focused on his work on the wind construct.>
312221.text1: <Riaani seems to be intently focused on his work on the wind construct.>

312224.text: Have you found what we need yet?
312224.text1: Have you found what we need yet?

312713.text: It can get boring up here, you know. I can only annoy that stuffy wretch Halaan so much before even that gets old.
312713.text1: It can get boring up here, you know. I can only annoy that stuffy wretch Halaan so much before even that gets old.

313248.text: Go on and have a seat near the fire and we can get started.

313249.text: All you need to start a camp of your own is a basic campfire. Cooks can generally teach you how to make one of those.

313250.text: Once your campfire is down, you can place all sorts of camp fixtures around it.

313251.text: Sufficiently skilled leatherworkers, for example, can place a tent like this one behind me.

313253.text: Every trade has something they can contribute to your camp, even fishermen!

313254.text: Then, all you need to do is have a seat near the fire and soak it all in. After a few minutes of resting, you'll gain various boons that will help you in your travels.

313255.text: If you just sit still and rest for a few more moments, you'll gain a benefit from having rested near the tent I have set up behind me.

313256.text: That's about the gist of it. Once you've gained your boon from resting near the fire, speak with me again.

313547.text: Greetings, traveler! I am Creeg Bothunk, the main supplier for the Darkspear Raiders. As you improve your standing with the Darkspear Raiders, I will be able to provide a variety of goods that you can use inside Darkspear Islands. Should you find yourself in need of item repair, I also provide those services.
313547.text1: Greetings, traveler! I am Creeg Bothunk, the main supplier for the Darkspear Raiders. As you improve your standing with the Darkspear Raiders, I will be able to provide a variety of goods that you can use inside Darkspear Islands. Should you find yourself in need of item repair, I also provide those services.

313648.text: The Nightclaw do not take kindly to reckless intruders. Tread carefully while in Shadowgale, $c.

314601.text: Wait, yes... this crystal! Valennia, is this...

314602.text1: ...a recall crystal! Used to record an important moment, no doubt.

314603.text: This is surely what the turncoat hoped to offer us in exchange for our protection.

314604.text1: The recall crystal is badly damaged, though. The recording is likely to be incomplete, so we must listen carefully.

314605.text: Activate it, Valennia. We need to learn as much as we can about what it contains.

314606.text1: ...do not delay. Muster our forces to march immediately. The pylons are key and...the wards...come down. This is...

314607.text1: ...quickly. With our forces.....will be exposed.....my ritual must not....

314608.text1: I alone am.....this task....the Windlord will.......our voices.....he will come.....we must not fail!

314609.text1: The crystal is too damaged to play any further, I am afraid.

314610.text: Wards... what is this about wards, Valennia?

314611.text1: The anchor pylons keep us suspended in this realm, but they also act as wards! The Shal'nan once spoke of this. They keep us shielded from...

314612.text: ...whatever else is out there in Skywall. Spirits save us... this is her plan. Bring down the wards and let her 'Windlord' in!

316076.text:
We paladins must earn our place amongst our Forsaken kin each day, lest we be judged as fanatics like the Scarlet Crusade. The light is not simply a tool of our foes, but a conduit for our righteous fury! It is in our devotion to the Dark Lady and the love of our home that we may channel the light to bring justice to our enemies.

The Banshee Queen keeps a close eye on us. Let her. She will see that our resolve shall never waver. We are Forsaken!

316310.text: It is vital that we learn more about what the cult is planning, and with the turncoat dead, the information may have died with him...

316321.text1: What business do you have in the Echo Isles, $c?

316364.text1:
I suppose that is true. I and the rest of my elites used to belong to an order known as the Empyrean Blades. We were the personal guard of our former leader, the Shal'nan. 

In the current, uncertain times we do what we can to help lead the peacekeepers' citizen militia, since we are the closest thing to professional soldiers left on Zephras.

316366.text1:
<Valennia looks away briefly before looking hesitantly back in your direction.>

The Shal'nan was the very best of us. It was he who stood up for our people against madness and oppression in Eldre'Thalas nearly ten thousand years ago. It was the Shal'nan who led us across the uncharted sea to escape the murderous vengeance of our ancient enemies.

It was the Shal'nan who brokered the pact of friendship with the wind spirits that allowed us to ascend to Skywall... and survive.

He was ever the servant leader to his people, even after he abdicated his position of power and retired.

316461.text: Be careful, $c. There are cultists nearby.

316796.text: Words are like arrows. Once loosed, you cannot call them back.

317261.text: It's good to see you again, Danitha. It's only been a few years, but it feels like an ocean of time has passed.

317262.text1: Indeed it does, Leonid. I've enjoyed our correspondence, but it pleases me that you finally made the trip out to Bandarion Keep in person.

317263.text: I am glad I came to see what you've built here. Garek would be proud. This was no social call, though, Danitha. Surely you know that...

317264.text1: Ah, so we are cutting straight to the point, then?

317265.text: Yes. Have you considered Lord Tyrosus's offer? The Argent Dawn is prepared to welcome you and your people with open arms.

317266.text1: I'm sorry, Leonid, but I must decline. Much has changed but the Forsaken are still the people we swore to protect.

317267.text: But they fear and hate you, Danitha. Surely you know that? Among the Argent Dawn your connection to the light would be an asset. You would be highly valued!

317268.text1: No, Leonid. Our place is here. Our fledgling order must find our identity amongst our kind. I know how you feel about the Forsaken... that our 'condition' is something to be cured.

317269.text1: I reject that notion. This is who we are now, and we will make the Forsaken see that we are not what they think we are. We can be of service to Lordaeron again.

317270.text: Very well, Danitha. Just take care of yourselves. Many Forsaken cannot let go of the pain they suffered at the hands of the living wielders of the light. Their mistrust of paladins runs deep.

317271.text1: That is why it is so important that we stay.

317273.text1: Enough of this talk. I want to speak of the good times. Garek would have wanted that for us.

317287.text: They named it Bandarion Keep. I wonder what Garek would make of that?

You've earned a degree of trust amongst the Nightclaw, $c. We don't have much to offer you as a reward, but we have managed to scavenge a number of crafting plans from the ruins of Ban'aethal.

The magesmiths of Ban'aethal were widely regarded to be the best artisans in all of the Skyborne Isles. The Nightclaw are naturalists, not crafters, so these records are of little use to us.

Continue to prove yourself to be a valuable ally, and I would make these secrets available to you.

Yes, I am the renowned trader who magnanimously fed the uh, starving... children...? ...of the Undercity during the recent war with the Scourge. Yes, I am the visionary businessgob and logistical genius who single-handedly armed the resistance and allowed our Dark Lady to found her nation of smelly corpses... um, I mean, "Forsaken."

Yep, I'm him. Glix Xizzix. I'd be happy to sign an autograph. For a small fee, of course.

What am I doing here running a barbershop, you ask? Well I got one word for you, bub--diversification. You've got to keep your revenue streams diversified!

324145.text1: All of the skyborne islands became destabilized and began to move apart a few years ago. If that wasn't bad enough, now large pieces of Zephras are beginning to fall away. It's hard to imagine your home falling into the sky, but that is my reality now.

324561.text: She dares make threats against us after her lackeys massacre our people in the highlands?

324562.text: I don't know who is more dangerous, the Al'Aketh, or the sky-cursed Windshapers! So be it. If she is not willing to resolve this with civility, we will not hesitate once the current crisis is over.

325066.text: I have the finest meats in Orgrimmar.

325825.text: Mind yourself in the presence of the Warchief, $c. The Kor'kron will suffer no insolence or insult here.

325827.text:
<Nazgrel grunts as he sizes you up.>

High elves, here in Orgrimmar. I'd never bet on such a thing happening in my lifetime, but at this point nothing is surprising to me.

Yes, the Warchief instructed me to draft up instructions for you. Take this letter and follow the instructions within. Conduct yourself with honor and show due deference when you meet with our leaders, elf.

Once you've finished your journey, return to the Warchief.

325829.text:
Muln Earthfury has told me much of the Windshapers and I am proud to open the lands--and skies--of Mulgore to your people.

The tauren and the Skyborne are both children of this land. Kalimdor. 

I hope that your people are able to find what they are looking for here and that you are able to save your homeland. In the meantime, it is my hope that you are able to learn more of the land that your ancestors used to call home.

Please make yourself at home here in Thunder Bluff, and may the Earth Mother bless your journey.

325830.text: I am Vol'jin, of the Darkspear. Do you be friend, or enemy?

325832.text:
Ah yes, I heard of the Windshapers. It be good to be meetin' you now.

You know, my people been fighting elves for thousands of years. If you be half as fierce as your cousins from Darnassus or Quel'Thalas, the Darkspear would be glad to call you friend.

I be wishin' you well in your travels, $c. We Darkspear know all too well what it's like to have no home, so I hope you be finding what your people need to save yours.

325835.text1:
I've heard of you. Windshapers. Wayward children of ancient Eldre'Thalas.

I once would have called you kin--albeit distant kin. Now I have no more in common with elfkind than I have with any of the other living races. All I value from any creature that draws breath is how well they may further the goals of the Forsaken. Make yourself useful to my people, and you will be welcome in our lands.

Go. Explore the Undercity as you like and enjoy its comforts, such as they are. Just remember, nothing escapes my notice within my own domain.

327804.text1:
<The wolf turns its head to regard you as you draw near. Even through the visor on its helm, you can feel its gaze as it studies you. It sniffs you gently, and after a moment lets out a low but not unfriendly growl in recognition. 

 
It stands up straighter, seemingly to show off the heavy armor adorning its body. The freshly polished metal gleams, even under a coat of Durotar dust kicked up by the hot winds. 

Something within you stirs and you sense that this wolf approves of your bravery and would be proud to bear you as its friend and rider.>

327805.text: <As you approach this wolf it shakes its great head; its armor glints gently against its ashen fur.>

327806.text: <The wolf stands tall and strong, even with the added weight of the armor.>
327806.text1:
<Just as the freshly hewed timbers of a cedar tree fade from red to grey, so too has this timber wolf's fur changed with maturity. Its once boisterous personality is focused, and it stands tall and strong, even with the added weight of the armor. 
 
Its long tail still wags in familiarity as you approach and lets out a knowing whine. Through the glowing enchantment of the helmet's visor, you see its eyes shine with determination; its thirst for adventure is undiminished. 

After a moment it lets out an excited growl. You get the sense that this wolf admires your adventurous spirit and is impressed by all the challenges you have surmounted. It would gladly accept you as a rider and companion.>

329335.text: Once a nomadic people, the tauren roam the endless plains of the Barrens, hunting the mighty kodo.

329336.text: Scattered across the lands, the wandering tribes were united only by their common hatred for their sworn enemy--the marauding centaur.

329343.text: The vicious trolls that populate the numerous jungle isles of the South Seas are renowned for their cruelty and dark mysticism.

329349.text: Bound to the iron will of the tyrant Lich King, the vast undead armies of the Scourge seek to eradicate all life on Azeroth.
